A1.justification: Both readable PDFs describe the same MOSAIC work, with matching core equations and experiments. Both end with references and contain no appendix pages, although v1 refers to an unsupplied appendix and supplementary material.

before.justification: Sections 5-6 report original multi-view generation experiments on HM3D and MP3D scenes, including baseline comparisons and ablations in Tables 1-4.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and additionally reports a SceneTex comparison on an eight-scene subset and further qualitative reconstruction results.

M1.justification: The multi-channel DDIM optimization, depth-weighted projection loss and late pixel-space refinement are retained in Eqs. 14-19. Added explanations of per-pixel weights and the encoder clarify existing operations without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both use 16 HM3D and 5 MP3D scenes with 2,011 depth/pose/caption triplets. The eight-scene subset and additional illustrated scenes remain within the existing text-guided indoor generation and reconstruction coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds SceneTex as an evaluated comparator in Figure 3 and Table 1, with corresponding MOSAIC results on an eight-scene subset. Warp-Inpaint, MVDiffusion, SceneCraft and Text2Room remain.

E3.justification: Section 5 introduces a separate eight-scene evaluation for SceneTex and MOSAIC because full SceneTex evaluation is considered impractical. Existing metrics and dataset totals remain unchanged; newly stated trajectory and overlap details do not establish revisions to the retained experiments.

E4.justification: v3 adds TSDF reconstruction case examples in Figure 4 and expands qualitative consistency and ablation examples in Figures 3 and 5. The quantitative loss-removal, key-frame selection and view-count analyses remain unchanged in Tables 3-4.

E5.justification: Section 6.1 newly states that SceneTex produces nearly identical textures across seeds. This is limited qualitative seed-related reporting: neither version provides seed identities, run counts, uncertainty estimates or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds eight-scene subset results, including SceneTex KID 0.10536 versus MOSAIC 0.06547. Previously tabulated scores are retained. Section 6.1 corrects MVDiffusion's prose KID from 0.0640 to 0.0364, matching its unchanged table entry; additional qualitative reconstruction, runtime and diversity findings are reported.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, projection-objective argument and conditional-variance derivation in Eqs. 1-21 are retained. Changes to terminology, loss notation and explanatory definitions do not introduce new assumptions, proofs or formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same substantive contributions: privacy-oriented depth-only generation, training-free cross-view optimization, depth and pixel losses, variance reduction with overlapping views, and superior fidelity and consistency.

C2.justification: v3 adds a mode-seeking explanation for SceneTex's limited diversity and contrasts it with DDIM sampling. It also explicitly links MVDiffusion's trained consistency module to generalization and prompt-following limitations and explains the runtime constraint behind the SceneTex subset.

D1.justification: New disclosures include approximately ten trajectories per scene, grayscale inputs for captioning, greater than 50% pixel overlap in the view-count analysis, and TSDF reconstruction. v3 also gives rough runtime comparisons and explicitly advertises code at the existing project URL.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to SceneTex, LucidDreamer, SDXL and rectified-flow transformers. Section 2 expands positioning against mesh-based texture optimization and trained multi-view diffusion while retaining the broader training-free research framing.

P1.justification: The introduction, contribution summary, related-work discussion, experimental setup and much of the results and ablation prose are substantially rewritten. Contributions become a compact paragraph, and explanations and captions are expanded, although the principal section sequence remains.

P2.justification: v3 substantially revises the visual presentation: Figure 3 gains a third scene and SceneTex row, a new reconstruction Figure 4 appears, ablation panels expand, and the alignment figure gains detailed annotations. Figures and tables are relocated, and Table 1 gains a separate subset comparison block.

improvement.justification: The separately reported SceneTex comparison, clearer procedural disclosures and expanded visual examples modestly improve empirical support and transparency. The gains remain limited: core results and theory are unchanged, the MOSAIC KID prose/table mismatch persists (0.0391 versus 0.03391), and new runtime and diversity assertions lack detailed supporting protocols.
